components.note: 钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 铁 iron, 钱 money, 银 silver; 钢 is steel.
冈 (gāng) gives the sound exactly: 钢 gāng, also in 刚 gāng and 纲 gāng.
珏 (two jades) — here the two 王 shapes suggest strings stretched over a body; 琴 is a string instrument.
今 (jīn) is only a loose sound hint for qín.

example.hanzi: 她每天练习钢琴一个小时。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān liànxí gāngqín yí gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: She practices piano for an hour every day.
example.fact: The piano was invented around 1700 by the Italian instrument maker Bartolomeo Cristofori, who called his creation a 'gravicembalo col piano e forte' — a harpsichord-like instrument that, unlike its predecessor, could play both softly and loudly depending on how hard a key was struck.

examples.hanzi: 我家有一架旧钢琴。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yí jià jiù gāngqín.
examples.english: We have an old piano at home.

examples.hanzi: 他的钢琴弹得非常好。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gāngqín tán de fēicháng hǎo.
examples.english: He plays the piano very well.

components.note: 会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 两位领导人在联合国会面。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi lǐngdǎorén zài Liánhéguó huìmiàn.
example.english: The two leaders met at the United Nations.
example.fact: The land beneath United Nations headquarters in New York is technically international territory, purchased in 1946 with an $8.5 million donation from John D. Rockefeller Jr. — worth well over $100 million today — specifically so the fledgling organization would have a permanent home.

examples.hanzi: 我们约好明天上午会面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yuēhǎo míngtiān shàngwǔ huìmiàn.
examples.english: We agreed to meet tomorrow morning.

examples.hanzi: 他们第一次会面是在机场。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen dì yī cì huìmiàn shì zài jīchǎng.
examples.english: They first met at the airport.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
阝 (town, from 邑) on the right — marks places and towns, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 邻 neighbour.
良 (liáng) hints at the sound: 郎 láng is close, as in 狼 láng, 廊 láng and 朗 lǎng.

example.hanzi: 电影里的邦女郎总是很神秘。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de Bāng nǚláng zǒngshì hěn shénmì.
example.english: The Bond girls in the movies are always mysterious.
example.fact: The James Bond film series began with 'Dr. No' in 1962 and has since grossed more than $7 billion worldwide, making it one of the highest-grossing film franchises ever made, spanning six different lead actors over more than 60 years.

examples.hanzi: 街上有一位穿红衣服的女郎。
examples.pinyin: Jiē shàng yǒu yí wèi chuān hóng yīfu de nǚláng.
examples.english: There is a young woman in red on the street.

examples.hanzi: 那位女郎正在咖啡店门口等人。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi nǚláng zhèngzài kāfēidiàn ménkǒu děng rén.
examples.english: That young woman is waiting for someone at the cafe entrance.

components.note: 复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.
亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你, 他, 做; 仇 is an enemy, a person you hate.
九 (jiǔ) is only a loose sound hint for chóu.

example.hanzi: 他花了十年时间策划复仇。
example.pinyin: Tā huāle shí nián shíjiān cèhuà fùchóu.
example.english: He spent ten years planning his revenge.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved into a stone stele around 1754 BC in ancient Babylon, is one of the earliest known written legal codes to formalize proportional retribution — the principle, later summarized as 'an eye for an eye,' that a punishment should match the harm done.

examples.hanzi: 他发誓要为父亲复仇。
examples.pinyin: Tā fāshì yào wèi fùqin fùchóu.
examples.english: He swore to take revenge for his father.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲的是一个复仇的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì yí ge fùchóu de gùshi.
examples.english: This movie tells a story of revenge.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 她大学主修数学。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué zhǔxiū shùxué.
example.english: She majored in mathematics in college.
example.fact: The number zero was developed as both a placeholder and a number in its own right by Indian mathematicians, most notably formalized by Brahmagupta around 628 AD, who also worked out rules for arithmetic involving zero and negative numbers centuries before these ideas reached Europe.

examples.hanzi: 我的数学成绩不太好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shùxué chéngjì bú tài hǎo.
examples.english: My math grades aren't very good.

examples.hanzi: 今天的数学作业很难。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de shùxué zuòyè hěn nán.
examples.english: Today's math homework is hard.

meanings: to go so far as to

components.note: 至 (arrive) — oldest form is an arrow landing on a mark: to reach. 至 sounds out 到 dào and 致 zhì, and sits in 室 shì room and 屋 wū.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 至于价格,我们可以再谈。
example.pinyin: Zhìyú jiàgé, wǒmen kěyǐ zài tán.
example.english: As for the price, we can discuss it later.
example.fact: Coined money is believed to have first appeared around 600 BC in the ancient kingdom of Lydia, in what is now western Turkey, using electrum, a naturally occurring pale gold-and-silver alloy. Standardized coinage made pricing and trading far more efficient than the barter and weighed-metal systems it replaced.

examples.hanzi: 至于他去不去，我不知道。
examples.pinyin: Zhìyú tā qù bu qù, wǒ bù zhīdào.
examples.english: As for whether he's going, I don't know.

examples.hanzi: 我已经同意了，至于其他的，你们决定吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng tóngyì le, zhìyú qítā de, nǐmen juédìng ba.
examples.english: I've already agreed; as for the rest, you decide.

components.note: 冏 (bright/window) — the lower part; dictionary treats it as the 'bright' hint. Meaning 'trade, business' is better remembered as a market (商店).
口 (mouth) — dictionary radical, as in 吃 eat. Memory aid: a shop-keeper's mouth calling out prices; 商量 is to 'talk it over'.

example.hanzi: 他在北京开了一家商店。
example.pinyin: Tā zài Běijīng kāi le yì jiā shāngdiàn.
example.english: He opened a shop in Beijing.
example.fact: 商 builds 商店 (shop), 商人 (merchant), 商业 (commerce), 商量 (to discuss). It also means 'quotient' in math. The Shang dynasty has the same character, and tradition says its people, after the fall, became traders.

examples.hanzi: 他是一名商人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng shāngrén.
examples.english: He is a businessman.

examples.hanzi: 我们先商量一下再决定。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān shāngliang yíxià zài juédìng.
examples.english: Let's discuss it first and then decide.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — marks bamboo and things woven or made from it, as in 笔 pen, 筷 chopsticks, 箱 box; 篮 is a woven basket.
监 (jiān) is a loose hint for lán; 蓝 lán shares it.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 他每天晚上都去打篮球。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshàng dōu qù dǎ lánqiú.
example.english: He goes to play basketball every evening.
example.fact: Basketball was invented in December 1891 by James Naismith, a Canadian physical education instructor in Springfield, Massachusetts, who needed an indoor winter activity for his students and nailed two peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony to serve as the original goals.

examples.hanzi: 我们周末去打篮球吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù dǎ lánqiú ba.
examples.english: Let's go play basketball this weekend.

examples.hanzi: 这个篮球场有很多人。
examples.pinyin: Zhège lánqiúchǎng yǒu hěn duō rén.
examples.english: This basketball court has a lot of people.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — two feet stepping upward: 登 is to climb or board, as in 登山 mountain-climbing.
豆 (dòu) is only a loose sound hint; 登 dēng also sounds out 灯 dēng and 凳 dèng.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.

example.hanzi: 请在前台登记你的信息。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài qiántái dēngjì nǐ de xìnxī.
example.english: Please register your information at the front desk.
example.fact: Compulsory civil registration of births and deaths in England and Wales began with the Births and Deaths Registration Act of 1836, which took effect in 1837. One motivation was administrative: officials needed reliable records to enforce the country's newly reformed Poor Law system.

examples.hanzi: 你需要先登记才能入住。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xūyào xiān dēngjì cái néng rùzhù.
examples.english: You need to register first before you can check in.

examples.hanzi: 我已经登记好了，可以进去了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng dēngjì hǎo le, kěyǐ jìnqù le.
examples.english: I've finished registering, so I can go in now.

components.note: 尚 (shàng) gives the -ang sound; also in 常 cháng, 偿 cháng, 堂 táng. The old form showed 旨 "tasty".

example.hanzi: 你尝一下这个菜。
example.pinyin: Nǐ cháng yíxià zhège cài.
example.english: Have a taste of this dish.
example.fact: 尝 is to taste: 尝尝 (try a bit), 品尝 (to savor), 尝试 (to try out). In literary speech 何尝 and 未尝 are rhetorical, as in 我何尝不想? ('how could I not want to?').

examples.hanzi: 你想尝尝我做的饺子吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng chángchang wǒ zuò de jiǎozi ma?
examples.english: Would you like to try the dumplings I made?

examples.hanzi: 我想尝试一下新的工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chángshì yíxià xīn de gōngzuò.
examples.english: I want to try a new job.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 骂 has two mouths 口口 — loud scolding.
马 (mǎ) — close sound: 骂 mà. 马 also sounds out 妈 mā and 蚂 mǎ.

example.hanzi: 妈妈骂了我一顿。
example.pinyin: Māma mà le wǒ yí dùn.
example.english: Mom scolded me.
example.fact: 骂 is to scold or swear: 骂人 (to swear at someone), 责骂 (to reproach), 挨骂 or 被骂 (to be scolded). 顿 is the measure word for a scolding, a meal, or a beating.

examples.hanzi: 别骂孩子,他不是故意的。
examples.pinyin: Bié mà háizi, tā bú shì gùyì de.
examples.english: Don't scold the child; he didn't do it on purpose.

examples.hanzi: 他被老板骂了一顿。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi lǎobǎn mà le yí dùn.
examples.english: He got scolded by his boss.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
寸 (hand, inch) — traditional 導 had 道 (road) plus 寸 (hand): a hand leading along a road; 道 dào is also a near-sound clue for 导 dǎo.

example.hanzi: 教练亲自指导每一位运动员。
example.pinyin: Jiàoliàn qīnzì zhǐdǎo měi yī wèi yùndòngyuán.
example.english: The coach personally guides every athlete.
example.fact: The English word 'mentor' comes from a character in Homer's 'Odyssey' — an old friend of Odysseus named Mentor, entrusted with guiding and advising his son Telemachus during Odysseus's long absence.

examples.hanzi: 老师在指导学生写作文。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài zhǐdǎo xuésheng xiě zuòwén.
examples.english: The teacher is guiding the students in writing essays.

examples.hanzi: 在老师的指导下，我进步很快。
examples.pinyin: Zài lǎoshī de zhǐdǎo xià, wǒ jìnbù hěn kuài.
examples.english: Under the teacher's guidance, I improved quickly.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.

example.hanzi: 请保护好你的眼睛。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎohù hǎo nǐ de yǎnjing.
example.english: Please protect your eyes.
example.fact: 护 appears in 保护 (to protect), 爱护 (to cherish), 护士 (nurse, 'protecting person') and 护照 (passport, 'protecting document'). 护肤 means skincare.

examples.hanzi: 医院的护士很耐心。
examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn de hùshi hěn nàixīn.
examples.english: The nurses at the hospital are very patient.

examples.hanzi: 出国要带护照。
examples.pinyin: Chūguó yào dài hùzhào.
examples.english: You need to bring your passport when you go abroad.

meanings: circles (as in a field of work)

components.note: 田 (field) — fields have boundaries, which is what 界 means.
介 (jiè) gives the exact sound; 介 also sounds out 价 jià.

example.hanzi: 这条河是两个省的分界。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé shì liǎng gè shěng de fēnjiè.
example.english: This river is the boundary between the two provinces.
example.fact: 界 rarely stands alone; it works as a suffix meaning 'a field or circle of people', as in 娱乐界 (the entertainment world) or 教育界 (educational circles), and it is also the second half of 世界 'world'.

examples.hanzi: 他是体育界的名人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì tǐyùjiè de míngrén.
examples.english: He is a celebrity in the sports world.

examples.hanzi: 世界杯每四年举行一次。
examples.pinyin: Shìjièbēi měi sì nián jǔxíng yí cì.
examples.english: The World Cup is held every four years.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and questions, as in 说, 请, 问; 诊 is a doctor questioning and examining.
㐱 (zhěn) gives the sound exactly: 诊 zhěn, also in 疹 zhěn.
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.

example.hanzi: 她在附近的诊所工作。
example.pinyin: Tā zài fùjìn de zhěnsuǒ gōngzuò.
example.english: She works at a nearby clinic.
example.fact: The Mayo Clinic grew out of a small private medical practice that Dr. William Worrall Mayo ran in Rochester, Minnesota, starting in the 1860s. It expanded rapidly after a devastating 1883 tornado forced the town to build a hospital to treat the injured, laying the groundwork for what became one of the world's largest medical centers.

examples.hanzi: 我感冒了，想去诊所看看。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, xiǎng qù zhěnsuǒ kànkan.
examples.english: I've caught a cold and want to go see a doctor at the clinic.

examples.hanzi: 这家诊所下午不开门。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā zhěnsuǒ xiàwǔ bù kāimén.
examples.english: This clinic isn't open in the afternoon.

meanings: (of a contagious disease etc) to spread
(of a style of clothing, song etc) popular

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 流 is flowing water.
㐬 (liú) — same sound — 流 is liú; 㐬 also sounds out 琉 liú and 硫 liú.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 这首歌去年非常流行。
example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē qùnián fēicháng liúxíng.
example.english: This song was very popular last year.
example.fact: The 1918 influenza pandemic, often called the 'Spanish flu' even though it likely didn't originate in Spain, is estimated to have infected about 500 million people — roughly a third of the world's population at the time — making it one of the deadliest outbreaks in recorded history.

examples.hanzi: 最近这种发型很流行。
examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn zhè zhǒng fàxíng hěn liúxíng.
examples.english: This hairstyle is very popular lately.

examples.hanzi: 冬天容易流行感冒。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān róngyì liúxíng gǎnmào.
examples.english: Colds spread easily in winter.

meanings: (fig.) person who has the potential to do the job

components.note: 木 (wood) — marks trees and timber, as in 树, 桥, 板; 材 is timber, then material.
才 (cái) gives the sound exactly: 材 cái, also in 财 cái.
斗 (dipper, measure) — measuring grain and liquids: 科, 斜, 升; 料 is rice 米 measured out, then material.

example.hanzi: 这座桥使用了新型材料建造。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo shǐyòngle xīnxíng cáiliào jiànzào.
example.english: This bridge was built using new materials.
example.fact: Graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice, is roughly 200 times stronger than steel by weight, yet it was first isolated in 2004 using little more than ordinary adhesive tape to peel thin flakes off a block of graphite — a discovery that earned its researchers the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics.

examples.hanzi: 做蛋糕需要准备哪些材料？
examples.pinyin: Zuò dàngāo xūyào zhǔnbèi nǎxiē cáiliào?
examples.english: What ingredients do you need to prepare for making a cake?

examples.hanzi: 我在整理考试要用的材料。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài zhěnglǐ kǎoshì yào yòng de cáiliào.
examples.english: I'm organizing the materials needed for the exam.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拿, 提; 揭 is to lift off a cover.
曷 (hé) is a loose hint for jiē; 喝 hē and 渴 kě share it.
日 (sun) — marks light and time, as in 明, 晴, 早; 晓 is dawn, when the sun comes up, and so to know.
尧 (yáo) is a loose hint for xiǎo; 烧 shāo and 浇 jiāo share it.

example.hanzi: 获奖名单将在晚会上揭晓。
example.pinyin: Huòjiǎng míngdān jiāng zài wǎnhuì shàng jiēxiǎo.
example.english: The list of winners will be announced at the evening event.
example.fact: Nobel Prize laureates are typically informed by a phone call just minutes before the public announcement, and under Swedish law the nominating committee's internal deliberations are sealed for 50 years before historians and the public can examine them.

examples.hanzi: 比赛结果明天就会揭晓。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài jiéguǒ míngtiān jiù huì jiēxiǎo.
examples.english: The competition results will be announced tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 谜底终于揭晓了。
examples.pinyin: Mídǐ zhōngyú jiēxiǎo le.
examples.english: The answer to the riddle was finally revealed.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.

example.hanzi: 考试前她感到非常不安。
example.pinyin: Kǎoshì qián tā gǎndào fēicháng bù'ān.
example.english: She felt very uneasy before the exam.
example.fact: The 'fight-or-flight' response — the rush of adrenaline that speeds up heart rate and sharpens alertness when facing a perceived threat — was first named and described by the American physiologist Walter Cannon in the 1920s.

examples.hanzi: 他一个人在外面，我有点不安。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí ge rén zài wàimiàn, wǒ yǒudiǎn bù'ān.
examples.english: He's out there alone, and I feel a bit uneasy.

examples.hanzi: 她脸上露出了不安的神情。
examples.pinyin: Tā liǎn shàng lùchū le bù'ān de shénqíng.
examples.english: An uneasy look appeared on her face.

components.note: 日 (sun) — dusk, when the sun sinks low, as in 暗 dark, 晚 evening; 昏 also means faint.
氏 here stands in for an older 氐 (low); 昏 hūn sounds out 婚 hūn.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迷 is losing one's way.
米 (mǐ) — near sound — 迷 is mí, the same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他因为车祸昏迷了三天。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi chēhuò hūnmíle sān tiān.
example.english: He was in a coma for three days because of a car accident.
example.fact: The Glasgow Coma Scale, still the standard tool doctors use worldwide to assess a patient's level of consciousness after a head injury, was developed by two neurosurgeons in Glasgow in 1974. It scores eye, verbal, and motor responses on a scale from 3 to 15.

examples.hanzi: 老人摔倒后昏迷了一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén shuāidǎo hòu hūnmí le yíhuìr.
examples.english: The old man fell and was unconscious for a while.

examples.hanzi: 医生说他还处于昏迷状态。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā hái chǔyú hūnmí zhuàngtài.
examples.english: The doctor said he is still in a coma.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 带, 帽: 帮 first meant the side of a shoe.
邦 (bāng, nation) gives the exact sound; 邦 itself means state or country.
巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 带, 帽: 帮 first meant the side of a shoe.
邦 (bāng, nation) gives the exact sound; 邦 itself means state or country.

example.hanzi: 你能帮帮我吗?
example.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāngbāng wǒ ma?
example.english: Can you help me out?
example.fact: The emergency number 911 was chosen for the United States in 1968 specifically because it was short, easy to remember on a rotary phone, and had never been used as a telephone exchange prefix or area code anywhere in the country, so it could be dialed unambiguously nationwide.

examples.hanzi: 请你帮帮他吧。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ bāngbang tā ba.
examples.english: Please help him out.

examples.hanzi: 我来帮帮你搬家。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lái bāngbang nǐ bānjiā.
examples.english: Let me help you move.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions done by hand, as in 找 look for, 拿 take, 抓 grab; 搜 is to search by hand.
叟 (sǒu) — same sound family — 搜 is sōu; 叟 also sounds out 艘 sōu.

example.hanzi: 警察搜了他的房间。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá sōu le tā de fángjiān.
example.english: The police searched his room.
example.fact: On its own 搜 is mostly used for physical searches or in the casual internet sense, as in 搜一下 'look it up'; in formal writing it usually appears in compounds like 搜索 (search) and 搜查 (search a place).

examples.hanzi: 我在网上搜了很久,但没找到。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài wǎng shang sōu le hěn jiǔ, dàn méi zhǎodào.
examples.english: I searched online for a long time but found nothing.

examples.hanzi: 你可以用手机搜索附近的饭馆。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng shǒujī sōusuǒ fùjìn de fànguǎn.
examples.english: You can search for nearby restaurants on your phone.

components.note: 午 (noon) — an old picture of a pestle or mallet, later borrowed for 'noon'. Memory aid: noon is when the sun stands straight overhead — 下午, 午饭.
夕 (evening) — 夕 is evening or dusk, as in 外, 多, 梦; 夜 is night.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 夜 is yè; 夜 also sounds out 液 yè.

example.hanzi: 他们工作到午夜才回家。
example.pinyin: Tāmen gōngzuò dào wǔyè cái huí jiā.
example.english: They worked until midnight before going home.
example.fact: Before railways forced standardization, most towns kept their own local time based on the sun, so noon in one city could be several minutes off from noon in a neighboring one. Britain adopted a single 'Railway Time' in 1840 to keep train schedules consistent, though it wasn't made the legal standard nationwide until 1880.

examples.hanzi: 我们聊到午夜才睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liáo dào wǔyè cái shuìjiào.
examples.english: We chatted until midnight before going to bed.

examples.hanzi: 午夜的街道很安静。
examples.pinyin: Wǔyè de jiēdào hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: The street at midnight is very quiet.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.

example.hanzi: 吸烟与肺癌密切相关。
example.pinyin: Xīyān yǔ fèi'ái mìqiè xiāngguān.
example.english: Smoking is closely linked to lung cancer.
example.fact: The 1964 U.S. Surgeon General's report was the first major government publication to formally conclude that smoking causes lung cancer, based on a review of more than 7,000 scientific studies by an independent advisory committee.

examples.hanzi: 这两个问题是相关的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge wèntí shì xiāngguān de.
examples.english: These two issues are related.

examples.hanzi: 如果你有相关经验，请告诉我们。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ yǒu xiāngguān jīngyàn, qǐng gàosu wǒmen.
examples.english: If you have relevant experience, please tell us.

components.note: 身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.
木 (wood) — marks trees and timber, as in 树, 桥, 板; 材 is timber, then material.
才 (cái) gives the sound exactly: 材 cái, also in 财 cái.

example.hanzi: 她通过跑步保持好身材。
example.pinyin: Tā tōngguò pǎobù bǎochí hǎo shēncái.
example.english: She stays in good shape by running.
example.fact: The marathon's official distance of 26.2 miles was fixed at the 1908 London Olympics so the race could start at Windsor Castle and finish directly in front of the royal viewing box in the stadium — a scheduling decision, not any ancient Greek precedent, which is a common misconception about the distance's origin.

examples.hanzi: 他的身材很高大。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēncái hěn gāodà.
examples.english: He has a tall, big build.

examples.hanzi: 她为了保持身材，不吃宵夜。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèile bǎochí shēncái, bù chī xiāoyè.
examples.english: To keep her figure, she doesn't eat late-night snacks.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk, as in 说, 语, 讲; 讽 is mocking talk.
风 (fēng) hints at the sound: 讽 fěng is close, as in 枫 fēng.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) on the right, as in 到, 别, 利; 刺 is to stab.
朿 (cì) — 朿 is a thorn and gives the sound — 刺 is cì, same syllable.

example.hanzi: 这部电影充满了政治讽刺。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng chōngmǎnle zhèngzhì fěngcì.
example.english: This movie is full of political satire.
example.fact: Jonathan Swift's 1729 essay 'A Modest Proposal,' which satirically suggested that impoverished Irish families sell their children as food to wealthy landlords, remains one of the most studied examples of sustained satire in English literature — a piece meant not literally but to expose the cruelty of contemporary economic policy.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事是对现实的讽刺。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi shì duì xiànshí de fěngcì.
examples.english: This story is a satire of reality.

examples.hanzi: 你这是在讽刺我吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè shì zài fěngcì wǒ ma?
examples.english: Are you mocking me?

components.note: 冫 (ice, two drops) — marks ice and cold, as in 冰, 冷, 冻; 凌 means ice, as in 冰凌, and being bitingly cold.
夌 (líng) gives the sound: 凌 líng, also in 陵 líng and 菱 líng.
日 (sun) — 日 is the sun and time of day, as in 明, 晚, 早; 晨 is early morning.
辰 (chén) — same sound — 晨 is chén, like 辰.

example.hanzi: 他凌晨四点就起床跑步了。
example.pinyin: Tā língchén sì diǎn jiù qǐchuáng pǎobùle.
example.english: He got up at 4 a.m. to go running.
example.fact: Human core body temperature typically reaches its lowest point of the day between about 4 and 5 a.m., a low in the circadian rhythm that also coincides with when most people feel the strongest biological pull toward sleep, regardless of how much rest they've had.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天凌晨才睡着。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān língchén cái shuìzháo.
examples.english: I only fell asleep in the early hours of yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 飞机在凌晨两点起飞。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī zài língchén liǎng diǎn qǐfēi.
examples.english: The plane takes off at 2 a.m.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 他, 做; 侮 is to insult a person.
每 (měi) is only a loose sound hint for wǔ.
辱 (rǔ) — to humiliate; as a part it sounds out 褥 rù and 溽 rù.

example.hanzi: 他在公开场合侮辱了对手。
example.pinyin: Tā zài gōngkāi chǎnghé wǔrǔle duìshǒu.
example.english: He insulted his opponent in public.
example.fact: Alexander Hamilton's fatal 1804 duel with Aaron Burr began after Hamilton refused to retract insulting remarks he had made about Burr's character. Dueling to defend one's honor after a public insult was still considered acceptable in parts of early 19th-century America, even though it was already illegal in the state where the duel took place.

examples.hanzi: 你不应该侮辱别人。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù yīnggāi wǔrǔ biéren.
examples.english: You shouldn't insult others.

examples.hanzi: 他觉得这句话是对他的侮辱。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde zhè jù huà shì duì tā de wǔrǔ.
examples.english: He felt this remark was an insult to him.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
山 (mountain) — marks hills and heights, as in 岛 island, 峰 peak, 崖 cliff; 岸 is a steep bank or shore.
干 (gān) is a loose hint for àn.

example.hanzi: 他们沿着海岸散步。
example.pinyin: Tāmen yánzhe hǎi'àn sànbù.
example.english: They walked along the coast.
example.fact: Norway's coastline, once every fjord and offshore island is measured, stretches for more than 100,000 kilometers — long enough to circle the Earth over twice — even though the country's land area is only about 385,000 square kilometers.

examples.hanzi: 我们开车去了海岸边的小镇。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kāichē qù le hǎi'àn biān de xiǎozhèn.
examples.english: We drove to a small town on the coast.

examples.hanzi: 海岸上有很多漂亮的贝壳。
examples.pinyin: Hǎi'àn shàng yǒu hěn duō piàoliang de bèiké.
examples.english: There are many pretty shells on the shore.

components.note: 齐 is the simplified form of 齊, a picture of ears of grain growing evenly level — hence 'even, together, complete'. Sound clue: 剂 jì, 挤 jǐ, 济 jì.
文 (writing) — the visible top part in the simplified form, not the meaning. Memory aid: neat writing in even lines is 整齐.

example.hanzi: 大家都到齐了。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu dào qí le.
example.english: Everyone has arrived.
example.fact: 齐 often follows a verb as a result complement meaning 'completely, all present', as in 到齐 or 备齐 (get everything ready). It is also the name of an ancient state in what is now Shandong, so you will see it in 齐国 and as a surname.

examples.hanzi: 菜都上齐了,大家吃吧。
examples.pinyin: Cài dōu shàng qí le, dàjiā chī ba.
examples.english: All the dishes are served, everybody dig in.

examples.hanzi: 把桌子摆整齐。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ zhuōzi bǎi zhěngqí.
examples.english: Arrange the tables neatly.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood and trees, as in 树, 林, 桌: 校 first meant a wooden frame or restraint.
交 (jiāo) is a close sound clue for xiào; 交 also in 较 jiào and 校 xiào.

example.hanzi: 我们在校门口见面。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài xiàoménkǒu jiànmiàn.
example.english: We'll meet at the school gate.
example.fact: Meaning 'school', 校 appears in compounds like 学校, 校长 (principal) and 校园 (campus). The same character read jiào means 'to proofread', as in 校对, so check the reading when you meet it.

examples.hanzi: 我们学校有一个大操场。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào yǒu yí ge dà cāochǎng.
examples.english: Our school has a big sports field.

examples.hanzi: 校长在会议上讲了话。
examples.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng zài huìyì shang jiǎng le huà.
examples.english: The principal gave a speech at the meeting.

components.note: 亚 (second, Asia) — the top part. Dictionary reading: an advance to the second (亚) day (日), hence 'advance'; 晋级 is to be promoted.
日 (sun) — the bottom part and radical, as in 明 bright. It marks days or time; in 晋 the sun rises to a higher level.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 给; 级 first meant the order of threads, then rank.
及 (jí) sounds exactly like 级; also 极 jí, 吸 xī.

example.hanzi: 这支球队晋级了半决赛。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì jìnjíle bànjuésài.
example.english: This team advanced to the semifinals.
example.fact: The FIFA World Cup has expanded its format several times since 1930; the 2026 tournament, co-hosted by the United States, Mexico, and Canada, will be the first edition to include 48 national teams instead of the 32 that competed in every tournament from 1998 through 2022.

examples.hanzi: 我们队没能晋级决赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duì méi néng jìnjí juésài.
examples.english: Our team didn't make it into the finals.

examples.hanzi: 他顺利晋级下一轮比赛。
examples.pinyin: Tā shùnlì jìnjí xià yì lún bǐsài.
examples.english: He smoothly advanced to the next round.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sighting along a straight line. 直 also sounds out 值 zhí and 植 zhí.
见 (see) — seeing and perceiving, as in 现, 看, 视: 觉 is to sense and become aware (jué), also "sleep" (jiào) in 睡觉.
The top is a shape of 学 (xué), a loose sound hint from the traditional 覺.

example.hanzi: 她的直觉总是很准。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhíjué zǒngshì hěn zhǔn.
example.english: Her intuition is always accurate.
example.fact: Psychologist Daniel Kahneman's 'System 1 and System 2' framework, popularized in his 2011 book 'Thinking, Fast and Slow,' describes intuition as a fast, automatic mode of thought that runs alongside a slower, more deliberate form of reasoning. Kahneman had already won the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 2002 for related work on decision-making.

examples.hanzi: 我的直觉告诉我，他在说谎。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zhíjué gàosu wǒ, tā zài shuōhuǎng.
examples.english: My intuition tells me he's lying.

examples.hanzi: 女人的直觉有时候很准。
examples.pinyin: Nǚrén de zhíjué yǒu shíhou hěn zhǔn.
examples.english: Women's intuition is sometimes very accurate.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 政府就此事作出了正式回应。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jiù cǐshì zuòchūle zhèngshì huíyìng.
example.english: The government made a formal response to this matter.
example.fact: The system of checks and balances written into the U.S. Constitution in 1787 was heavily influenced by the French philosopher Montesquieu's 1748 treatise 'The Spirit of the Laws,' which argued that dividing government power among separate branches was necessary to prevent any one part from becoming tyrannical.

examples.hanzi: 你要尽快作出决定。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào jǐnkuài zuòchū juédìng.
examples.english: You need to make a decision as soon as possible.

examples.hanzi: 他作出了很大的努力。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòchū le hěn dà de nǔlì.
examples.english: He made a great effort.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — words passed down through ten 十 generations of mouths — old; 古 also sounds out 姑 gū and 故 gù.

example.hanzi: 这是一座很古的城市。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí zuò hěn gǔ de chéngshì.
example.english: This is a very ancient city.
example.fact: 古 means 'of ancient times' and is used in compounds like 古代 and 古老, whereas 老 describes ordinary age. So an old building you simply find worn is 老房子, but a historic one is a 古建筑.

examples.hanzi: 这个古老的村子有一千年历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gǔlǎo de cūnzi yǒu yì qiān nián lìshǐ.
examples.english: This ancient village has a thousand years of history.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢研究中国古代历史。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yánjiū Zhōngguó gǔdài lìshǐ.
examples.english: He likes studying ancient Chinese history.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
罒 (net) — 罒 is a net, as in 罚, 置; 罗 is a net, and is mostly seen in 罗马 Rome.

example.hanzi: 保罗是我最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: Bǎoluó shì wǒ zuìhǎo de péngyǒu.
example.english: Paul is my best friend.
example.fact: The name Paul derives from the Latin 'Paulus,' meaning 'small' or 'humble,' originally used as a Roman family name (cognomen) rather than a given name. Despite its modest original meaning, it has remained one of the most consistently popular male names across the Western world for close to two thousand years.

examples.hanzi: 我同事叫保罗，他是美国人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tóngshì jiào Bǎoluó, tā shì Měiguó rén.
examples.english: My colleague is called Paul, and he's American.

examples.hanzi: 保罗周末想请我们吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Bǎoluó zhōumò xiǎng qǐng wǒmen chīfàn.
examples.english: Paul wants to treat us to a meal this weekend.

components.note: 广 (building) — 广 is a building or roof, as in 店, 床, 库; 废 is a ruined building, then discarded.
发 (fā) — loose hint — 废 is fèi, close in sound to 发 fā.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 这个旧电视已经是废物了,该扔掉了。
example.pinyin: Zhège jiù diànshì yǐjīng shì fèiwù le, gāi rēngdiào le.
example.english: This old television is already junk; it's time to throw it out.
example.fact: Recycling a single aluminum can saves enough energy to power a television for about three hours, because turning scrap aluminum back into new metal takes only about 5% of the energy needed to refine it from raw ore. That gap is why aluminum is one of the most economically worthwhile materials to recycle.

examples.hanzi: 别把废物放在楼道里。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ fèiwù fàng zài lóudào lǐ.
examples.english: Don't leave junk in the stairwell.

examples.hanzi: 他觉得自己是个废物。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde zìjǐ shì ge fèiwù.
examples.english: He feels like he's a good-for-nothing.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 日 is the sun — 暴 originally meant to expose to the sun (still in 暴露), then violent, as in 暴力.
雨 (rain) — marks weather and moisture, as in 雪, 雷, 雾; 露 is dew.
路 (lù) gives the sound exactly: 露 lù (dew) or lòu (reveal).

example.hanzi: 调查最终暴露了公司的财务问题。
example.pinyin: Diàochá zuìzhōng bàolù le gōngsī de cáiwù wèntí.
example.english: The investigation ultimately exposed the company's financial problems.
example.fact: X-rays were discovered by accident in 1895, when Wilhelm Röntgen noticed a screen glowing in his lab even though it was shielded from visible light. To convince skeptical colleagues the new rays were real, he exposed a photographic plate to his wife's hand, producing an image of her bones and wedding ring — the first X-ray photograph ever taken.

examples.hanzi: 他的秘密被朋友暴露了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de mìmì bèi péngyou bàolù le.
examples.english: His secret was exposed by his friend.

examples.hanzi: 皮肤不要长时间暴露在阳光下。
examples.pinyin: Pífū búyào cháng shíjiān bàolù zài yángguāng xià.
examples.english: Don't expose your skin to the sun for long periods.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks cloth and cords, as in 线, 红, 约; 绅 is a sash, worn by gentlemen.
申 (shēn) gives the sound exactly: 绅 shēn, also in 神 shén and 伸 shēn.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 他总是表现得像一位真正的绅士。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì biǎoxiàn de xiàng yí wèi zhēnzhèng de shēnshì.
example.english: He always behaves like a true gentleman.
example.fact: In Victorian England, being a 'gentleman' was defined less by wealth than by not having to work with one's hands for a living; owning land that produced passive income was the real marker of the class. That is why many cash-poor aristocrats still counted as gentlemen while some far wealthier factory owners did not.

examples.hanzi: 他对每个人都很有礼貌，像个绅士。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì měi ge rén dōu hěn yǒu lǐmào, xiàng ge shēnshì.
examples.english: He's polite to everyone, like a gentleman.

examples.hanzi: 这位绅士帮老太太提行李。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi shēnshì bāng lǎotàitai tí xíngli.
examples.english: This gentleman helped the old lady carry her luggage.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — a picture of a crawling worm; as a radical it marks insects and creepy-crawlies, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蜘 spider, 蛇 snake.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 花园里爬着一只绿色的虫子。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ pá zhe yì zhī lǜsè de chóngzi.
example.english: A green bug was crawling in the garden.
example.fact: Insects outnumber humans by roughly 200 million to one, and entomologists estimate their combined weight across the planet exceeds that of all wild mammals and birds put together. Ants alone are thought to weigh, in total, about as much as all humans on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 夏天晚上有很多虫子。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǎnshang yǒu hěn duō chóngzi.
examples.english: There are lots of bugs on summer evenings.

examples.hanzi: 菜叶上有几只小虫子。
examples.pinyin: Càiyè shàng yǒu jǐ zhī xiǎo chóngzi.
examples.english: There are a few little bugs on the vegetable leaves.

components.note: 台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and language, as in 说 say, 语 language, 话 speech; 词 is a word or phrase.
司 (sī) hints at the sound: 词 cí is close, and 司 also gives 饲 sì and 祠 cí.

example.hanzi: 演员忘记了下一句台词。
example.pinyin: Yǎnyuán wàngjì le xià yí jù táicí.
example.english: The actor forgot the next line.
example.fact: Shakespeare's Hamlet has more lines than any other character he wrote — nearly 1,500 — meaning whoever plays the role speaks for close to 40% of the entire play's running time, one of the most demanding memorization tasks in classical theater.

examples.hanzi: 这句台词太有名了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jù táicí tài yǒumíng le.
examples.english: This line is so famous.

examples.hanzi: 他把整部电影的台词都背下来了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhěng bù diànyǐng de táicí dōu bèi xiàlái le.
examples.english: He memorized all the lines of the whole movie.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
皿 (dish) — marks vessels, as in 盒 box, 盖 lid, 盆 basin; 盘 is a plate.
舟 (boat) here stands in for 般 (bān), which hints at pán, as in 搬 bān.

example.hanzi: 这条街是他们帮派的地盘。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē shì tāmen bāngpài de dìpán.
example.english: This street is their gang's turf.
example.fact: Wolves mark their territory with scent from glands between their toes and can defend a range spanning hundreds of square miles. Rival packs typically detect these scent markers long before any face-to-face encounter, which is how wolves avoid most physical fights over land.

examples.hanzi: 你不要闯进别人的地盘。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyào chuǎng jìn biéren de dìpán.
examples.english: Don't barge into someone else's territory.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司想扩大自己的地盘。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī xiǎng kuòdà zìjǐ de dìpán.
examples.english: This company wants to expand its turf.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
民 (people) — one old theory sees an eye pierced by a pointed tool, a mark of those with no rights; the meaning "ordinary people" is what to remember.

example.hanzi: 每个公民都有投票的权利。
example.pinyin: Měi gè gōngmín dōu yǒu tóupiào de quánlì.
example.english: Every citizen has the right to vote.
example.fact: In ancient Athens, citizenship was so restrictive that only free adult men born to two Athenian parents qualified for it. That single rule excluded the majority of the city's population — women, slaves, and resident foreigners — from any political voice at all, despite Athens's reputation as the birthplace of democracy.

examples.hanzi: 他在这个国家已经是合法公民了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhège guójiā yǐjīng shì héfǎ gōngmín le.
examples.english: He is already a legal citizen of this country.

examples.hanzi: 公民应该遵守法律。
examples.pinyin: Gōngmín yīnggāi zūnshǒu fǎlǜ.
examples.english: Citizens should obey the law.

meanings: to keep a firm grip on

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: to seize.
爪 (zhǎo, claw) is a close sound clue for zhuā and fits the meaning: grab with claws.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 经, 系: a pulled-tight cord. The top part is also in 坚 jiān (firm).

example.hanzi: 我们得抓紧时间完成任务。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen děi zhuājǐn shíjiān wánchéng rènwù.
example.english: We have to hurry and get the task done without wasting time.
example.fact: Geckos can support many times their own body weight while hanging upside down, thanks to millions of microscopic hair-like structures on their toes called setae. These exploit weak molecular attraction (van der Waals forces) rather than any sticky glue, letting the gecko grip and release instantly with each step.

examples.hanzi: 你得抓紧练习，比赛快到了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ děi zhuājǐn liànxí, bǐsài kuài dào le.
examples.english: You need to practice in earnest; the competition is coming up soon.

examples.hanzi: 他抓紧了扶手，生怕摔倒。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhuājǐn le fúshou, shēngpà shuāidǎo.
examples.english: He gripped the handrail tightly, afraid of falling.

meanings: seems on the face of it to be

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 外面看起来快要下雨了。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn kànqǐlai kuàiyào xiàyǔ le.
example.english: It looks like it's about to rain outside.
example.fact: The Müller-Lyer illusion, first described in 1889, makes two identical straight lines look like different lengths just by attaching arrow-like fins to their ends. A ruler proves the lines are equal, but the brain's habit of interpreting the fins as depth cues keeps overriding what is actually there.

examples.hanzi: 他看起来很累。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlai hěn lèi.
examples.english: He looks very tired.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜看起来好吃，闻起来也很香。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài kàn qǐlai hǎochī, wén qǐlai yě hěn xiāng.
examples.english: This dish looks tasty and smells good too.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸭 duck, 鹅 goose, 鸽 pigeon; 鸡 is a chicken. 又 only replaces the old sound part.
虫 (insect, creature) — small animals and insects, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake, 虾 shrimp: 蛋 is the egg of a creature.

example.hanzi: 妈妈煮了两个鸡蛋当早餐。
example.pinyin: Māma zhǔ le liǎng gè jīdàn dāng zǎocān.
example.english: Mom boiled two eggs for breakfast.
example.fact: A hen's egg is naturally much stronger against pressure from the top and bottom than from the sides, thanks to its arched shell shape. That design lets a nesting hen sit on and turn a whole clutch of eggs without cracking them, even though her body weight far exceeds what a single shell could take from a sideways push.

examples.hanzi: 我早餐喜欢吃一个鸡蛋。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǎocān xǐhuan chī yí ge jīdàn.
examples.english: I like to eat an egg for breakfast.

examples.hanzi: 冰箱里还有六个鸡蛋。
examples.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ hái yǒu liù ge jīdàn.
examples.english: There are still six eggs in the fridge.

components.note: 歹 (bone, death) — marks death and decay, as in 死 die, 殆; 残 is damaged or cruel.
戋 (jiān) is a loose hint for cán; it appears in 钱 qián, 浅 qiǎn and 线 xiàn.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart, as in 想, 思, 念; 忍 is a blade 刃 over the heart — enduring pain.
刃 (rèn) — near sound — 忍 is rěn; 刃 is a blade with an edge marked by a dot.

example.hanzi: 这种对待动物的方式非常残忍。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng duìdài dòngwù de fāngshì fēicháng cánrěn.
example.english: This way of treating animals is extremely cruel.
example.fact: The Colosseum in ancient Rome could reportedly be flooded to stage mock naval battles, called naumachiae, complete with warships and condemned combatants fighting to the death for the crowd's entertainment. Historians believe this required an elaborate underground system of channels to flood and drain the arena floor on demand.

examples.hanzi: 他对待敌人非常残忍。
examples.pinyin: Tā duìdài dírén fēicháng cánrěn.
examples.english: He treats his enemies very cruelly.

examples.hanzi: 这个决定对孩子太残忍了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège juédìng duì háizi tài cánrěn le.
examples.english: This decision is too cruel to the child.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摄 is taking hold, then capturing on camera, as in 拍摄.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 像 is a person's likeness.
象 (xiàng, elephant) gives the exact sound; 象 first meant elephant, then "image".
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 电脑上方装了一个摄像头。
example.pinyin: Diànnǎo shàngfāng zhuāng le yí gè shèxiàngtóu.
example.english: A webcam is installed above the computer.
example.fact: The world's very first webcam was pointed not at a person but at a coffee pot in a University of Cambridge computer lab in 1991, so researchers down the hall could check whether it was full before making the walk. The feed stayed live on the early internet until the pot was finally retired in 2001.

examples.hanzi: 门口的摄像头拍到了他。
examples.pinyin: Ménkǒu de shèxiàngtóu pāi dào le tā.
examples.english: The camera at the door caught him on film.

examples.hanzi: 开视频会议前要先打开摄像头。
examples.pinyin: Kāi shìpín huìyì qián yào xiān dǎkāi shèxiàngtóu.
examples.english: You need to turn on the camera before starting a video meeting.

components.note: 关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 请把门关上,外面太冷了。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ mén guānshàng, wàimiàn tài lěng le.
example.english: Please close the door — it's too cold outside.
example.fact: Revolving doors were patented in 1888 specifically to cut heat loss at building entrances, since they never stand fully open the way a hinged door does. Studies of modern building entrances have found a well-used revolving door can lose several times less heated or cooled air than an equivalent swinging door.

examples.hanzi: 出门前记得把窗户关上。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén qián jìde bǎ chuānghu guānshàng.
examples.english: Remember to close the windows before leaving.

examples.hanzi: 睡觉前请把灯关上。
examples.pinyin: Shuìjiào qián qǐng bǎ dēng guānshàng.
examples.english: Please turn off the light before going to sleep.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 造 is to go and make something.
告 (gào) is a loose sound clue (-ao); also in 浩 hào, 靠 kào.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth, as in 地, 城; a mold was made of clay, so 型 is a model or type.
刑 (xíng) — same sound — 型 is xíng, like 刑.

example.hanzi: 她今天的发型造型很特别。
example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān de fàxíng zàoxíng hěn tèbié.
example.english: Her hairstyle today has a very distinctive design.
example.fact: Male peacock spiders perform an elaborate, colorful courtship dance, fanning out iridescent flaps on their abdomen and waving specialized legs in a precise sequence. The display exists purely to shape a visual impression striking enough to persuade a much larger, potentially cannibalistic female not to eat him.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的装修造型很时尚。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de zhuāngxiū zàoxíng hěn shíshàng.
examples.english: This shop's decor has a very stylish look.

examples.hanzi: 这个玩具的造型像一只小熊。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wánjù de zàoxíng xiàng yì zhī xiǎo xióng.
examples.english: This toy is shaped like a little bear.
